Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{5\pi }{4},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-\frac{5\pi }{4}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{4})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{4}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
